newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss find more owners for Holocaust accounts.
newsitem.headline: Swiss find more owners for Holocaust accounts.

text.p: Swiss banks have matched 10 million Swiss francs ($6.8 million) in dormant wartime wealth to specific Holocaust victims and identified owners for another seven million in unclaimed assets, a Swiss banker said on Tuesday.
"Some 17 million Swiss francs in dormant assets, 10 million of Holocaust victims, were identified in Swiss banks by the end of May 1997," Swiss banking ombudsman Hanspeter Haeni said in a statement.
"He has found legitimate owners for these 17 million," a Swiss Bankers Association spokeswoman said.

It was a big step forward since last November, when Haeni said the hunt for unclaimed wealth in secretive Swiss banks' vaults had found valid claims for only 1.6 million francs, of which only 11,000 francs was held by Jews.
Swiss banks have put the total of all dormant accounts -- not just those opened by Jews -- at 38.7 million Swiss francs.
This was far below the billions of dollars of Holocaust victims' money that Jewish groups have alleged Swiss banks were hoarding, a figure the banks have dismissed as wildly inflated.
Banks gave Haeni the job of coordinating the search for accounts opened at Swiss banks during or shortly before World War Two and which have been unclaimed for at least 10 years.
An independent auditing panel agreed last year by banks and Jewish groups is also checking banks' books for any such unclaimed wealth that may still remain.

Jewish groups had been disappointed by Haeni's original findings in November and have pinned their hopes on the search by the panel of independent auditors headed by former U.S. central bank chief Paul Volcker.
Swiss bankers have said they do not expect to find much more unclaimed wealth in their vaults more than 50 years after World War Two ended. ($ = 1.460 Swiss Francs)
